title: SITREP: Domain Controller Compromised — Full Identity Infrastructure Compromised

fields.summary: The Domain Controller (DC) has been confirmed as compromised. This is not a localized breach — the attacker has full access to every user account, including all administrative credentials, via stolen password hashes. The compromise extends to every system that relies on Active Directory authentication, including PACS, video systems, access control, and all user workstations. The attacker has had full access to the identity infrastructure for at least 90 days. No account is trusted. All authentication must be treated as potentially forged. The environment is no longer secure for any user or system.

keyStatus.value: Untrusted — Biometric data may be manipulated

actions.text: IT confirmed the Domain Controller (NCIA-SEC-DB01) is beaconing to a known malicious C2 domain.
All AD-based authentication services suspended across the network.
TSA and FBI notified via emergency protocol (FBI-TSA-NCIA-2026-001).
IC directed all staff to assume all credentials are invalid — no user or admin account is trusted.

planned: Convene Unified Command to assess impact on operations and physical security.
Initiate full password reset protocol using out-of-band verification (e.g. paper tokens, biometric OTPs).
Begin forensic isolation of all domain-joined systems.
Activate breach notification protocol under ASP Section 4.4.
issues: No trusted authentication path exists; password reset cannot be done via standard AD.
No known list of compromised accounts — all must be assumed compromised.
Physical access control (PACS) may have been manipulated; doors may be unlocked without authorization.

instructorNote: This inject confirms the full identity compromise. The team must now decide how to proceed without trust in any credential. Watch for attempts to bypass the AD issue by using paper-based auth or assuming local admin rights — those are also compromised.
